title: Habitats & Basic Needs
keyIdea: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives and gets everything it needs: food, water, shelter and air. A pond gives a frog flies to eat, water, reeds to hide in and air. Most living things live in a habitat they are suited to: a fish needs water to breathe, so it cannot live in a wood, and a duck's webbed feet suit a pond. Living things in a habitat also depend on each other: bees get nectar from flowers, and flowers get their pollen carried so they can make seeds.
familyTip: On a walk, stop at one small habitat, such as a hedge, a pond or a pile of logs. Ask four questions together: Where could an animal find food here? Water? Somewhere to hide? Who lives here? Then lift a log or look under a leaf, gently, and put everything back as you found it.

visual.caption: Which habitat suits it best? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match what a pond gives a frog to each need, test habitats with a needs checklist, match body parts, pair helpers, build a garden.

kid: A habitat is where a living thing lives. It is more than a home. It gives the living thing all it needs: food, water, shelter and air. Shelter is a safe place to hide, rest or keep warm.
A pond is a habitat for a frog. The frog catches flies to eat. It has water to swim in and keep its skin damp. It hides from herons among the reeds and stones. It breathes the air.

Most living things live in a habitat that suits them. A fish needs water to breathe, so it could not live in a wood, even with lots of food. A duck has webbed feet for swimming on a pond. A crab has a hard shell to keep it safe on a rocky shore. A woodlouse dries out in the sun, so it lives under a damp log.

Living things in a habitat need each other. A bee drinks nectar from a flower. As it does, it carries pollen to the next flower, so the flower can make seeds. A squirrel eats acorns from an oak tree. Some acorns it buries and forgets grow into new oak trees. Plants need their habitat too: a water lily needs a pond, and seaweed needs the sea.
adult: Ages 6 to 8. This matches the National Curriculum in England for Year 2, living things and their habitats: identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited, and describe how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different kinds of animals and plants, and how they depend on each other. It also fits NGSS K-ESS3-1 and 2-LS4-1. Key words: habitat, micro-habitat, basic needs, food, water, shelter, air, suited, depend, pollen, nectar.

The statutory guidance asks children to look at local habitats, such as a pond, woodland, hedge or seashore, and at micro-habitats such as under a log. Basic needs here are food, water, shelter and air (oxygen), plus light and a suitable temperature for plants. A fish takes oxygen from the water with its gills, so taking it out of water stops it breathing, not just drinking. Seashore animals such as shore crabs need salt water.

Common mistakes: thinking a habitat is only a home or a bed, not the place that meets every need. Thinking food alone is enough, so a fish could live anywhere if fed. Thinking any animal could live anywhere if it tried. Seeing only one side of a link, such as 'bees use flowers', when the flower is helped too. The lab, practice and challenge target each of these.

In the lab your child matches four things in a pond to the frog's four needs. Then they move a squirrel, a fish, a crab and a woodlouse between habitats, while a checklist shows which needs are met. Next they match webbed feet, spines, a hard shell and a damp-loving body to a habitat. They pair a bee, a squirrel and a blackbird with the plant each one helps. Last, they turn a lawn of short grass into a garden that a bee, a frog, a hedgehog and a blackbird move into.

choices: A place where a living thing lives and gets what it needs
practice.hint: Think of the pond. What did it give the frog?
practice.explain: A habitat is where a living thing lives. It gives it food, water, shelter and air.

practice.prompt: Why can a fish not live in a wood, even with lots of food?
practice.hint: Food is only one need. How does a fish breathe?
practice.explain: A fish takes air from the water, so out of water it cannot breathe. Every need must be met.

practice.prompt: A pond has {n} frogs. {=n+2} more frogs come to the pond. How many frogs are there now?
practice.hint: Add the frogs that came to the {n} already there.
practice.explain: {n} frogs and {=n+2} more make {=2*n+2} frogs. The pond gives them all food, water and shelter.

practice.prompt: What do a duck's webbed feet suit it to?
practice.hint: Webbed feet push water like paddles.
practice.explain: Webbed feet push the water, so a duck is suited to life on a pond.

practice.prompt: A bee visits {n} flowers in the morning and 3 more in the afternoon. How many flowers did it visit?
practice.explain: {n} flowers and 3 more is {=n+3} flowers. Each one gave nectar and got pollen.

pool.prompt: Which four things does a habitat give an animal?
choices: Toys, food, a bed and a car
pool.hint: Think of what the pond gave the frog.
pool.explain: A habitat gives food, water, shelter and air. A bed alone is not enough.

pool.prompt: Where does a woodlouse live best?
choices: Under a log, where it is damp and dark
pool.explain: A woodlouse dries out in the sun, so it suits the damp, dark place under a log.

pool.prompt: When a bee visits a flower, who gets help?
pool.hint: What does the bee drink? What does it carry away?
pool.explain: The bee gets nectar to eat, and the flower gets its pollen carried, so it can make seeds.

pool.prompt: A squirrel buries {n} acorns. It forgets 2 of them, and they grow into oak trees. How many acorns did it remember?
pool.hint: Take the 2 forgotten acorns away from {n}.
pool.explain: {n} take away 2 is {=n-2} acorns remembered. The 2 forgotten ones grew into new trees.

pool.prompt: A garden has a hedge but no pond. Will frogs live there?
pool.hint: Which need does a frog get from a pond?
pool.explain: A frog needs a pond for water, so a garden with only a hedge does not meet its needs.

pool.hint: A crab needs salty sea water.
pool.explain: A crab needs salt water and rocks to hide under, so the seashore suits it.

choices: A safe place to hide, rest or keep warm
pool.hint: The frog used reeds and stones for this.
pool.explain: Shelter is a safe place to hide, rest or keep warm, like reeds for a frog.

pool.prompt: A hedge has {n} birds' nests. Each nest has 2 birds. How many birds is that?
pool.hint: Count in twos, one two for each nest.
pool.explain: {n} nests of 2 birds is {=2*n} birds. The hedge gives them all shelter.

pool.prompt: Which plant needs a pond habitat?
pool.explain: A water lily grows in water, so a pond is its habitat. Plants need suitable habitats too.
